transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

My mind just won’t slow down—ideas are racing all the time and I can’t keep my thoughts straight anymore. It's just gotten so overwhelming, and I feel like I'm constantly falling behind because of it.
Have you struggled with these racing thoughts constantly since childhood, or do they come and go in distinct phases?

No, this isn't something from childhood; it actually started about a year and a half ago when I threw myself into trying to become a CNA supervisor. It definitely comes and goes in phases, and it gets much worse when I'm in those high-energy stretches where I'm barely sleeping.
During those times when you are barely sleeping, do you feel exhausted and tired, or do you find that you still have plenty of energy and don't feel the need to sleep?
I don't feel tired at all during those times, even if I only get three or four hours of sleep. I wake up feeling completely wired and full of energy, as if I don't even need any more rest.
On the other hand, do you also experience periods where you feel very down, exhausted, or lose interest in the things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I do have periods where it feels like all the life has gone out of me. I'll just sit on the couch for hours and ignore phone calls, and I completely lose interest in my painting and crochet. All my projects just sit there in unfinished piles because I can't bring myself to care enough to touch them.
When you experience these high-energy phases with very little sleep, how long do they typically last? Do they go on for several days, a week, or even longer?

They last much longer than just a few days or a week. In fact, these high-energy phases have been a major, ongoing part of my life for almost the entire year and a half since I started pushing for the supervisor role. They only seem to ease up for a very brief time before flaring right back up again.
When you experience those low periods where you lose interest in your hobbies and sit on the couch, how long do they typically last at a time?
I'm not quite sure exactly how long those low periods last. I haven't really tracked the exact number of days or weeks, because I tend to completely lose track of time when I'm feeling that down.
During those low periods when you feel like all the life has gone out of you, do you also experience significant changes in your appetite, feelings of worthlessness, or thoughts of self-harm?

No, I don't really experience those specific things—my appetite is mostly normal, and I don't have thoughts of self-harm or feeling worthless. It's more just that I feel completely flat and empty inside, like I just don't have the energy or care to do anything at all.

During your high-energy phases, have you ever made impulsive decisions or taken risks that caused serious problems in your life, such as reckless spending, risky behavior, or major conflicts with others?

I don't really do things like reckless spending, but I definitely take on way too much at once by signing up for too many extra shifts and classes. I've also had major conflicts, like snapping at people, raising my voice at my supervisor, and accusing a colleague of sabotaging my training. That tense incident actually led to my hours being cut and me being referred here for this evaluation.
Before this past year and a half, did you ever experience milder ups and downs in your mood, or was your mood completely stable throughout your life before then?

Before a year and a half ago, I felt pretty stable and balanced with my usual routine of painting, gardening, and taking quiet walks. I don't really remember having any notable ups and downs like this back then.
Have you experienced these low, empty periods on multiple different occasions over the past year and a half, or has it only happened once?

I'm not really sure about having distinct 'low' episodes that come and go. It feels more like a constant flatness or loss of energy on many days, like the life has just gone out of me, rather than separate, distinct periods of depression. Because of that, I'm really not sure how to count them.
When you experience that flatness or loss of energy, does it ever last continuously for at least two weeks at a time, where you feel that way nearly every day?
I'm not quite sure of the exact timing of those feelings. It happens on a lot of days, but it's hard to say if it lasts for two weeks straight because everything just seems to blend together.
During those flat periods when you lost interest in things, did you find it difficult to perform your job or manage your daily responsibilities at home?

Yes, it was incredibly hard to get anything done during those flat periods. At home, I would just sit on the couch for hours, ignore phone calls, and let my art and crochet projects pile up. My performance at work and school also slipped significantly—my charting became so unreliable that my supervisor cut my hours, and I fell behind in my evening classes.

During the past year and a half, have you had any periods lasting at least a few weeks where your mood felt completely normal and you felt like your usual self, in between the high-energy and flat phases?

No, I haven't really had any times where I felt completely normal or like my old self over the last year and a half. Even when the high-energy phases ease up briefly, I still feel keyed up, or my mood drops to just 'so-so' while I continue to hear those whispered voices and feel like people are trying to sabotage me.
Have you ever experienced hearing those whispered voices or feeling like others are trying to sabotage you during a time when your mood felt relatively normal and stable for at least two weeks?

Yes, that actually happened this past winter during a long stretch where my mood and energy had leveled off and felt relatively normal, or just 'so-so'. Even though my mood wasn't super high or low, I was still hearing those whispered voices when I was alone and felt convinced that people at work were secretly changing things to sabotage me.
During that period last winter when your mood was relatively stable, did those whispered voices and feelings of sabotage last for at least two weeks continuously?

Yes, those voices and the feeling of being sabotaged definitely lasted continuously for well over two weeks during that time. Even though my mood and energy had leveled off to just "so-so," those experiences kept happening day after day without any break.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent manic symptoms (racing thoughts, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, and severe irritability) and periods of depressive-like flat affect. Additionally, she experiences active psychotic symptoms, including auditory hallucinations (whispering voices) and persecutory delusions (beliefs of workplace sabotage). Crucially, these psychotic symptoms persisted continuously for over two weeks during a period when her mood and energy had leveled off to normal ('so-so'), meeting the key diagnostic requirement for Schizoaffective Disorder (F25) over a bipolar mood disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia.
